targetWords.definition: Actual means that something is real or true.
targetWords.example: This is the actual sword that the King owned, not a fake one.

targetWords.definition: To amaze someone is to surprise them very much.
targetWords.example: ■The news in the paper amazed Jack.

targetWords.definition: £5? A charge is the price to pay for something.
targetWords.example: The charge for the shirts was $15.00.

targetWords.definition: To comfort someone means to make them feel better.
targetWords.example: I wanted to comfort my friend after I heard the bad news.

targetWords.definition: To contact someone is to speak or write to them.
A customer is a person who buys something at a store.
targetWords.example: The customer put a few items in a bag.

targetWords.definition: To deliver something is to take it from one place to another.
targetWords.example: ■The man delivered Chinese food to my house.

targetWords.definition: To earn means to get money for the work you do.
targetWords.example: ■He earns his living as a chef in a great restaurant.

targetWords.definition: Gates are usually made of metal or wood.
targetWords.example: ■We want to put up a wooden gate around our house.

targetWords.definition: To include something means to have it as part of a group.
targetWords.example: ■Does this meal include a soft drink? 134

targetWords.definition: To manage something means to control or be in charge of it.
targetWords.example: ■I had to manage the meeting myself.

targetWords.definition: A mystery is something that is difficult to understand or explain.
targetWords.example: The path on the map was a complete mystery to me. 1

targetWords.definition: To occur means to happen.
If A is the opposite of B, A is completely different from B.
targetWords.example: The opposite of black is white.

targetWords.definition: A plate is a flat round thing that you put food on.
targetWords.example: I put my plate down so I could put some food on it.

targetWords.definition: — I received a present on my birthday.
A reward is something given in exchange for good behavior or work.
targetWords.example: He was given a reward for his excellent performance.

targetWords.definition: To set something is to put it somewhere.
targetWords.example: Please set the dice down on the table.

targetWords.definition: To steal is to take something that is not yours.
targetWords.example: The men tried to steal money from the bank.

targetWords.definition: A thief is someone who quietly takes things that do not belong to them.
targetWords.example: A thief broke into our home and took my mother's jewelry.

story.title: A Better Reward
story.passage:
Jenny delivered food for a restaurant. She read the newspaper and said, " Uh

oh." There was a story about a thief. He stole food, and no one had seen him.

Even the police couldn't catch him. Jenny was a little scared. She worked close to

that area.

The newspaper included a message from the police: " If anything strange

occurs, call us. If you help us catch the thief, you'll earn a reward."

Jenny talked to Jim. He managed the restaurant. " Do you know about the

thief?"

"Yes," he said. " But he steals more than one person can eat. And why haven't

the police stopped him yet? It's a mystery. If you see him, contact the police.

Don't run after him."

Jenny drove to a customer's house. She left her car and opened the gate to

the house. But then sheheard anoise by her car. She yelled, "Thief!" She wasn't

scared. She wanted thereward! Shedid the opposite of what Jim told herto do.

" Hey," she yelled. " Get back

here!" She set the food on the

ground and ran to her car.

But the thief had already left with

the food. Jenny followed a noise

around the corner. She was amazed.

She saw a dog and some puppies.

They were eating her food! They

looked thin and scared. "The actual

thief is just a dog. She's feeding her

puppies," she said. "That's why she

steals so much food."

Jenny felt bad. She tried to comfort the dogs with another

plate of food. Then she took them back to the store. Everyone

there took a puppy home. Jenny called the police. She told them

there was no real thief.

Jenny didn't do it to receive the reward anymore. She said, " It

was just a dog. But there's no charge for catching this 'thief,'"

she said. " My new dog is a better reward."

A man who tells a mystery

questions.question: Why did Jenny decide to run after the thief?

options.text: She wanted to earn the reward.
She knew that there was no actual thief.
She always did the opposite of what Jim said.
She wanted to charge a customer for that food.
He tried to comfort Jenny with food.
He told Jenny that she should contact the police.
He wrote a story that included a message from the police.
He received a reward because he managed the store.

questions.question: How did Jenny act when she heard the noise?

options.text: She was amazed by the noise.
She followed it around the corner.
She ran through the gate to get away from it.
She set the food on a table and ran to her car.
